title: Platform systems & services: roadmap, runbooks, dashboards, and team wiki
author: Priya Nair
content:
Purpose
This page is the canonical eng-platform reference for systems & services inventory, how-tos, dashboards and alerts, runbooks, retrospective notes, and the near-term (12–18 month) roadmap. It’s intended for platform engineers, SRE, and anyone operating or integrating with the Redwood Platform services. Use linked subpages for detailed runbooks and component designs.

Scope
- Services covered: platform control plane (control-plane-api), routing (router-service), autoscaler (burst-autoscaler), cluster manager (cluster-mgr), metric ingestion (metric-proxy), cost-and-billing pipeline (cost-pipeline), and the observability stack (otel-collector, prometheus, grafana).
- Exclusions: model runtime/serving internals (see eng-serving-runtime), customer-specific private deployment docs (see eng-private-deployments).

Owner & Contacts
- Platform Director (doc owner): Priya Nair (priya.nair@redwood.com)
- Primary oncall channel: #platform-oncall (PagerDuty escalation as configured)
- Component owners: see table below (owner emails are on the team wiki).

Systems & Services Inventory (summary)
- control-plane-api — REST API for route management, model pinning, and rollout config. SLO: 99.95% availability per region. Owner: platform-api team.
- router-service — Smart request router (policy-based). SLO: 99.9% request routing success. Alert: routing-error-rate > 0.5% over 5m.
- burst-autoscaler — Multi-tenant autoscaling with burst pools. SLO: scale-to-capacity within 90s for 95th percentile of scale events.
- cluster-mgr — Cluster lifecycle, spot/ondemand management, node draining and capacity forecasting.
- metric-proxy — Ingests telemetry, forwards to prometheus remote write and cost pipeline. Key for SLO calculation.
- cost-pipeline — Batch and streaming jobs that produce per-route cost reports and tokens-per-second accounting.

How-tos (quick operational recipes)
1) Deploy a control-plane change (canary + rollback):
   - Create PR and link ADR/acceptance tests.
   - Merge to main -> CI builds image -> push to registry.
   - Trigger canary rollout: `platformctl rollout start control-plane-api --canary 10% --duration 15m`
   - Monitor `grafana/dashboard/control-plane-api` (latency, error-rate, CPU, memory).
   - If errors spike above threshold (see alerts): `platformctl rollout abort control-plane-api --canary-id <id>`
   - For rollback to previous stable: `platformctl rollback control-plane-api --to-tag <stable-tag>`

2) Add a new alert to the platform alerting stack:
   - Author Prometheus rule in `ops/alerts/platform-rules/` using the rule template (see `alert-template.yaml`).
   - Run `make prom-lint` and open PR.
   - Request oncall review and deploy to staging alert-rule namespace.
   - After 24h in staging, promote to production; update Runbook linking the rule.

Dashboards & Alerts (operational summary)
- Canonical dashboards:
  - Platform Overview (grafana/dashboard/platform-overview) — top-level SLO heatmap, route errors, regional capacity.
  - Autoscaler Health (grafana/dashboard/autoscaler-health) — queue length, scale events, failed scale attempts.
  - Cost & Throughput (grafana/dashboard/cost-throughput) — tokens/sec per-route, cost per-token, batching efficiency.
  - Ingest & Telemetry (grafana/dashboard/ingest-overview) — metric proxy latency and drop rate.

- Key alerts (attached to the `platform-oncall` rotation):
  1) control-plane-api-high-error (P1): error-rate > 1% for 5m AND increase of 3x baseline — PagerDuty P1. Runbook: control-plane-api-high-error.
  2) router-service-misroute (P1): routing-error-rate > 0.5% for 5m — investigate policy changes and fallback configs.
  3) autoscaler-failed-scale (P1/P2): failed scaling events > 3 in 10m — inspect cloud provider throttles, spot interruption rate.
  4) metric-proxy-drop (P2): prometheus remote write error-rate > 0.2 — may impact SLO reporting and alerting.
  5) cost-pipeline-lag (P2): batch jobs lag > 2hr — notifications to finance and product.

Alert routing & dedupe rules
- P1 alerts -> PagerDuty: #platform-oncall (primary) -> #platform-eng (notification).
- P2 alerts -> #platform-ops (Slack) and email to owner list.
- Deduplication: alerts with the same `instance` label are suppressed for 10m to avoid alert storms.

Runbooks (high-level playbooks)
A. High latency for control-plane-api (runbook id: RB-PLAT-001)
1) Confirm: check grafana `control-plane-api/latency` for p50/p95/p99 spike and prometheus query: `histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le))`
2) Check error-rate and recent deploys: `platformctl deployments list --since 1h`
3) If related to a recent deploy: rollback to last stable tag (see How-tos step 1).
4) If CPU-bound: scale replicas: `k scale deployment control-plane-api --replicas X -n platform`.
5) If datastore latency (DB): open DB incident runbook, add DB owner to the Slack thread.
6) Postmortem required if impact > 30m or customer-facing degradation.

B. Router-service misrouting / high routing-error-rate (RB-PLAT-002)
1) Validate config propagation: `kubectl logs router-service-<pod> -n platform | grep "policy load"`
2) Check policy-store for malformed rules. If rollback needed: `git revert <policy-commit>` then `platformctl config apply --force`
3) Temporary mitigation: flip router to passive-fallback mode: `platformctl router set-mode passive`
4) Engage policy owners and file a follow-up task.

C. Autoscaler failed scale (RB-PLAT-003)
1) Inspect scale events and provider API errors in `cluster-mgr` logs.
2) If provider throttling: increase request concurrency backoff or request quota bump.
3) If spot interruptions are causing instability: move critical lanes to on-demand pools and notify capacity team.
4) Escalate to SRE lead if >3 failed scales in 30m.

Incident retrospectives (summary of recent learnings)
- Incident: 2025-11-12 control-plane partial outage (4 regions degraded for ~45m)
  - Root cause: deprecated DB index and a malformed migration that surfaced under high write load.
  - Impact: SLO breach for control-plane-api (4 hours rolling window).
  - Actions completed: reverted migration, restored index, added migration preflight checks, and added a canary write test for DB migrations.
  - Open improvements: automated schema migration dry-run in CI (owner: eng-infra, ETA: 2026-04), and a cross-team ops playbook for DB schema changes.

- Retro themes and action items (ongoing):
  1) Strengthen deploy guardrails: require smoke tests for all DB migrations. (owner: platform-api)
  2) Improve observability on write-heavy operations — add per-table write metrics (owner: metric-proxy)
  3) Update runbooks with clearer escalation matrix and SLA-driven postmortem triggers (owner: SRE)

Roadmap (12–18 months, prioritized)
- Q2–Q3 2026 (near-term):
  - Feature: Canary traffic shadowing — ability to mirror 100% production traffic to canary without impacting upstream SLOs. (owner: platform-api)
  - Feature: Autoscaler policy engine v2 — workload-aware scaling with predict-and-prewarm. (owner: cluster-mgr)
  - Operational: Prometheus scaling improvements and remote-write sharding to reduce ingestion lag. (owner: observability)

- Q4 2026 – Q1 2027 (mid-term):
  - Feature: Multi-region active-active control plane (pilot with 2 customers). (owner: platform-ops)
  - Feature: Dynamic billing telemetry per-route (low-latency cost attribution). (owner: cost-pipeline)
  - Operational: Full runbook library migration to the new runbook portal with integrated postmortem templates. (owner: eng-sre)

Risks & mitigation
- Risk: Increased alert noise during large infra changes. Mitigation: require alert staging and timeboxed mute windows implemented by change-management.
- Risk: Cost growth from autoscale misconfiguration. Mitigation: cost-safety limits and automated rollback of autoscale policies that exceed expected spend delta.

Team wiki pointers (where to go next)
- Platform runbook index: /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/platform-runbook-index
- Deployment how-tos and CLI: /confluence/eng-platform/how-tos/deployments
- Dashboards: /confluence/eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/index
- Roadmap board & epics: /confluence/eng-platform/roadmap/2026-q1-q4

Maintenance & governance
- Review cadence: this doc and linked runbooks should be reviewed quarterly by eng-platform leads.
- Runbook ownership: each runbook must include a named oncall reviewer; SRE ensures runbooks are tested twice per year via game-days.

Appendix: Useful commands
- `platformctl status --component router-service --since 15m`
- `k logs -l app=router-service -n platform --since=10m`
- `make prom-lint && make prom-deploy`

If you find missing or stale information, open a PR against this page or reach out in #platform-docs.
